A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Shortcut-aware multimodal reward-modeling work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-distribution experiments, shortcut diagnostics, downstream Best-of-N evaluations, and training-data-size and visual-patch analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds cross-distribution experiments with InternVL2-2B and InternVL2-4B.

M1.justification: Equation (7) removes the erroneous leading minus sign from the weighted objective, since the component loss already contains a negative logarithm. The dual-branch architecture, SFC weighting, gradient detachment, and inference procedure remain unchanged. This establishes a correction to the stated objective, not an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions use VLFeedback, POVID, and RLHF-V, plus MM-Vet, LLaVA-Bench-in-the-Wild, and MMHal-V downstream evaluations. The added model sizes retain these tasks and distributions. Medical-imaging and background-bias examples are conceptual, not evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain standard MM-RMs, text-only controls, and the downstream policy without Best-of-N selection. The new capacity analysis uses smaller versions of the existing standard-MM-RM comparator. Newly cited debiasing and Group DRO methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix G extend the cross-distribution evaluation from InternVL2-8B to 2B and 4B configurations. Existing dataset splits, metrics, training hyperparameters, and downstream Best-of-N procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a model-capacity sensitivity analysis examining whether scaling resolves generalization problems and whether shortcut-aware training benefits smaller models. Existing length-bias, case-study, training-data-size, and visual-patch analyses are retained; the patch analysis moves from Appendix C to D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing unbiased Best-of-N estimator is unchanged, moving from Appendix D to H.

E6.justification: Figures 10–11 add 2B and 4B accuracy matrices, supporting average out-of-distribution gains of 6.4 and 6.8 percentage points over their matched standard MM-RMs. The original 8B results, downstream Table 2 scores, and earlier supplementary results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds a conditional-entropy approximation for optimized losses and derives SFC approximately equal to 1/(2−rho), where rho measures normalized conditional visual information. It also expresses normalized SFC weighting as a distribution shift. These are limited supporting derivations and a heuristic DRO connection, without a new generalization theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about text-only shortcuts, dynamic sample reweighting, improved generalization, and downstream scalability. The added experiments support those existing claims.

C2.justification: New appendices connect SFD to worst-group accuracy, explain weighting through visual information and robust optimization, and discuss possible image-only or background-only proxies. Appendix G interprets capacity scaling as complementary to shortcut mitigation. These extend the supporting interpretation without replacing the original explanation; the alternative proxies remain untested.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same data-partitioning instructions, model construction, frozen components, patch limit, and hyperparameter table. No new hardware, runtime, code-access, or data-access information accompanies the added model-size experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bahng et al., Jung et al., Sagawa et al., Nam et al., and Chaudhuri et al., extending connections to debiasing, worst-group accuracy, and Group DRO. The existing related-work section and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The original narrative is largely retained. Changes include limited experiment-heading and paragraph edits, new appendix cross-references and discussion sections, acknowledgements, and updated publication and correspondence information. Existing appendices are relabeled around the additions.

P2.justification: Figures 10–11 add model-size heatmaps, including redisplayed 8B results. Existing figures and tables retain their designs, with localized placement changes such as Figure 7 and Table 2 moving between columns. The visual-patch figure is relocated with its appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the training-objective sign and reduces dependence on a single model size by demonstrating benefits at 2B and 4B. Added discussion clarifies the weighting rationale and diagnostic context. The gain remains limited: the entropy/DRO arguments are conditional or heuristic, alternative proxies are untested, and the original benchmark results and central claims remain unchanged.
